evidence_sources.rationale: spells/invoke/plan.md is the current normative Plan mode contract for purpose, parts, composability, validation, execution handoff, and authority limits.
spells/invoke/README.md supplies current Invoke lifecycle ownership, evidence ceilings, downstream consumers, and Plan-wide gates.
spells/invoke/PLAN-ARTIFACT-BOUNDARIES.md is the current source for artifact ownership, executable hierarchy, ordering, source-truth, choreography, navigation, and execution-stop rules.
The current template explicitly retires IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md in favor of Work Pack and Implementation Layering while retaining historical decomposition and handoff semantics.
The template confirms the independent governance role, layer decisions, promotion evidence, deferrals, and non-regression conditions of Implementation Layering.
The template is the current detailed contract for Work Pack source truth, internal planning units, validation, exact selection, closeout, and execution-entry boundaries.
The template confirms Execution Pack choreography, layer-mapped waves, task and SWU references, and its medium/high-complexity scope.
The completed package preserves delivery-slice, ordering, validation, failure, ownership, and handoff concepts but cannot establish current Plan execution or authority.
The completed layering artifact demonstrates layer questions, promotion evidence, deferrals, and stop decisions whose meanings remain current.
The completed Work Pack demonstrates task, SWU, gate, blocker, validation, navigation, and current-state semantics without supplying current readiness.
The completed Execution Pack demonstrates wave choreography, dependency ordering, parallelization boundaries, and exact unit selection.
The validation artifact preserves distinctions among authoring validity, structural coherence, mutation readiness, integrated closeout, and remaining residue.
The artifact supplies historical evidence for SWU atomicity, recomposition, first-unit narrowness, exact selection, blocking, and escalation semantics.
The ledger preserves independently owned blocker and gap meanings, repair routes, severity, and resolution state.
The result preserves the distinction between a complete authoring package, blocked mutation readiness, selected-unit handoff, and lifecycle ownership.
The thin context supplies the historical authoring, bundle, admission, and evidence-state layer, reassessed without accepting its old closure claims.
The thin closure receipt records historical dispositions only; it supplies no current closure or authority.
The thin source materializes four evidence-bearing concepts whose boundaries remain relevant but incomplete for Plan itself.
The generated definitions preserve historical concept boundaries and relations but are neither current nor canonical.
The receipt demonstrates the historical distinction between deterministic production and independent admission without proving current Plan correctness.
The expanded context's eighteen-term inventory is the candidate semantic denominator and is reassessed item by item against current sources.
The expanded closure preserves historical term dispositions but supplies no current semantic or authority decision.

The expanded source supplies the explicit candidate concepts, relations, and boundaries; current evidence requires corrected directions, additional direct source-truth edges, one companion split, and one closeout boundary.

facets.rationale: Invoke Plan is the bounded subject: it translates one approved Design into governed executable planning without performing implementation or assuming downstream authority.

The model retains Work Pack, Implementation Layering, layers, slices, waves, tasks, SWUs, detail contracts, validation, gates, blockers, gaps, closeout, execution entry, and Execution Pack as independently testable parts or invariants.
Direct structured edges preserve source-truth consumption, work-pack-to-wave-to-task-to-SWU composability, layer governance, validation dependencies, exact selection, and choreography contrast.
Authored, admitted, readiness-proved, accepted, and execution-authorized states remain separate and require current evidence from the owner of each axis.

Validation obligations, Plan gates, blocker and gap classification, atomicity, recomposition, navigation, closeout, and readiness stop conditions are materialized in relations and boundary conditions.
The model distinguishes preparation of exact SWU, closeout, route, scope, evidence, and selection contracts from execution, acceptance, mutation admission, and lifecycle work.

Plan owns planning artifacts and handoff context; approved Design remains upstream authority, and Task Session, Spellcraft, Sigil Development, acceptance owners, and readiness owners retain their downstream authority.

includes: The single machine-readable source of author-controlled Work Pack meaning, planning policy, exact frontier, routes, scopes, validation contracts, and readiness configuration.
A direct binding to the exact approved Design consumed by Plan.
excludes: Derived human views, calculated digests, validator verdicts, owner acceptance, readiness receipts, execution receipts, and mutation results.
conditions: An execution-candidate Plan has exactly one authored machine source.
Every derived Plan view and execution projection must be produced from the same validated source bytes without semantic invention.
The source must bind one exact approved Design predecessor and must not silently revise it.

includes: The complete deterministic set of required Plan artifacts and its producer evidence.
excludes: Independent bundle admission, owner acceptance, implementation readiness, execution authority, task execution, and product mutation.
conditions: Every member must derive from the same exact Plan authoring source and producer run.
Missing, substituted, or semantically inconsistent members prevent a complete candidate claim.

includes: Independent replay of the exact source, exact bundle-inventory comparison, structural checks, freshness checks, and declared consumer results.
excludes: Semantic invention, Design revision, promotion, owner acceptance, implementation readiness, execution admission, and mutation.
conditions: The admitting identity must be independent of the bundle-producing identity.
Admission applies only to the exact current source and bundle bytes it checked.
Admission does not satisfy any later readiness, acceptance, or execution-authority gate.

includes: Separate authored, admitted, readiness-proved, owner-accepted, and execution-authorized axes with exact evidence references.
excludes: A collapsed generic PASS, inferred registry release, inferred mutation readiness, inferred acceptance, and inferred execution permission.
conditions: Every positive axis requires current evidence issued by the owner responsible for that axis.
A passing authored or admitted Plan can open only its matching evidence axis.
Byte drift, semantic change, route change, frontier change, validation-contract change, or stale evidence invalidates the affected claim.

includes: The governed translation of approved Design into implementation objective, decomposition, ordering, validation, gates, blockers, gaps, current planning state, and execution handoff.
Ownership of Work Pack authoring, Implementation Layering composition, SWU execution contracts, validation strategy, and bounded handoff context.
excludes: Revising approved Design decisions, editing upstream artifacts without approval, source-code mutation, task execution, glossary promotion, owner acceptance, publication, deployment, and downstream lifecycle completion.
Pre-generating execution-time context packs.
conditions: Normal Plan activation requires approved stable Design outputs, source references, an explicit delivery boundary, an implementation objective, validation strategy, and required companion availability or recorded deferral.
Missing approved inputs, contradictory delivery boundaries, acceptance-critical blockers, or unavailable required companions block Plan.
Plan must stop or escalate when required implementation details cannot be resolved without a product, semantic, scope, authority, protected-effect, cost, or risk decision.

includes: The source of truth for executable planning and current execution readiness.
Objective, delivery slices, task and SWU manifests, validation strategy, blockers, gaps, gates, output mode, active layer window, current state, and navigation to split artifacts.
excludes: Layer-governance philosophy and promotion evidence owned by Implementation Layering.
Duplicated deep task-local detail when split task contracts exist.
conditions: Work Pack, wave files, task files, and execution projections must agree; disagreement keeps the Work Pack gate blocked until reconciliation.
Low complexity may remain reviewable in one file; scope above the low-complexity limits requires split output and an Execution Pack.
Task, wave, SWU, and source-contract links must make the first executable unit navigable without repository search.
Mutation-capable execution requires a passing Work Pack gate and all applicable validation, atomicity, closeout, and readiness conditions.

includes: The source of truth for L0-L3 layer governance, layer decision questions, promotion evidence, explicit deferrals, nested-layer policy, and non-regression guarantees.
excludes: Task execution detail, task or SWU status tracking, and SWU implementation contracts.
conditions: Every Plan has one global Implementation Layering companion.
Later layers must preserve guarantees proven earlier.
Deferred scope remains explicit and cannot be silently pulled into an earlier layer.
Promotion decisions must cite evidence rather than preference.

includes: One coherent delivered outcome with dependencies, layer and wave mapping, and its validation boundary.
excludes: Execution ordering, detailed task instructions, and SWU atomicity decisions.
conditions: Every slice must produce one or more Plan tasks with explicit dependencies.
Every slice must have a validation strategy and expected evidence.

includes: One L0-L3 decision boundary with its decision question, minimum working unit, included and deferred scope, exit evidence, and promotion decision.
excludes: Task implementation details, execution ordering, and execution-status ownership.
conditions: L0 proves the smallest useful concept; L1 addresses repeatability or hardening; L2 addresses governance, reliability, validation, or degraded modes; L3 addresses packaging, scale, release, or rollout.
Promotion must cite evidence from the previous layer.
A failed promotion gate stops, narrows, pivots, remediates, or defers advancement.

includes: Execution ordering, layer mapping, wave goal, entry gate, included tasks and SWUs, dependency order, parallelization boundaries, exit evidence, and promotion evidence.
excludes: Detailed implementation specifications and source-of-truth task or SWU definitions.
conditions: Each wave must name its layer, layer question, promotion evidence, and exit gate.
Wave order must respect task and SWU dependencies.
Medium and high complexity plans require explicit layer-mapped waves and baseline wave W0.
Parallel units require disjoint write scopes or an explicit merge plan.

includes: One implementation responsibility with objective, slice and layer mapping, source contracts, dependencies, blocker state, write scope, SWUs, done criteria, validation, handoff, synchronization, and completion evidence.
excludes: Global Plan rationale, unrelated task state, and placeholder-only task files.
conditions: Every task belongs to one or more waves.
A split task file must be a useful task-local execution contract.
Medium and high complexity execution tasks require implementation-detail contracts.
Non-exempt execution tasks must list their SWUs; closure-only exemptions require the declared VERIFY, AUDIT, SIGNAL, or READINESS identity.

includes: One primary behavior or decision, exactly one parent task, dependencies, source anchors, related context, explicit write scope, done criteria, acceptance evidence, validation surface, execution-owner recommendation, handoff note, and expected result shape.
The preferred bounded execution and subagent handoff unit.
excludes: Multiple independently verifiable behaviors bundled for file sharing, task order, or convenience.
Execution-time context packs generated during Plan authoring.
conditions: Every SWU belongs to exactly one task and one or more ordering waves.
Each SWU must have one independently reviewable acceptance boundary and documented split analysis.
If candidate children can pass independently, the SWU must be split.
The first selected SWU must be the narrowest reversible trust-building step.
Unknown or duplicate IDs, invalid exemptions, or missing dependencies, context, scope, evidence, done criteria, validation, owner, or handoff data block execution.

includes: Purpose, owned decision, inputs, outputs, data model or state, ordered algorithm or pseudocode, interface and data-flow behavior, precedence or transition rules, edge cases, failure modes, constraints, acceptance checks, and validation evidence.
excludes: New product or architecture decisions belonging to Design and unrelated implementation choices.
conditions: Medium and high complexity execution tasks require this contract.
A task title or outcome alone is not execution-ready.
Missing acceptance-critical detail blocks Plan or escalates to the decision owner; useful non-critical detail may remain only as an owned gap with a repair route.

includes: An exact validation target, timing, command or reviewable check, expected result, evidence output, and failure owner.
excludes: Unrunnable aspirations, decorative technique citations, and future evidence represented as a current PASS.
conditions: Validation timing must be pre-execution, post-produce, or closeout and must match when the required artifact can exist.
A post-produce validator or create output must not be required to exist before its producing SWU runs.
Every delivery slice and non-exempt SWU requires reviewable validation evidence.
Failed acceptance-critical validation stops mutation-capable handoff.

includes: A named target, required current evidence, accepted outcomes, decision, blocker causes, and repair or escalation route.
excludes: Implicit approval, preference-only promotion, generic PASS, stale receipts, and prose or template resemblance used as proof.
conditions: Acceptance-critical blockers keep the gate blocked.

Missing required companions, inconsistent layer mappings, missing validation, task-shaped SWUs, failed atomicity, failed first-unit narrowness, missing navigation, overlapping parallel writes without a merge plan, incomplete closeout, or stale readiness evidence block mutation-capable handoff.
Distill block prevents mutation-capable routing; Distill flag requires named gaps, owners, and repair paths.
Work Pack gate status must be pass before mutation-capable execution.

includes: A known cause, affected claim or transition, dependencies, owner, impact, next action, and repair route.
excludes: Non-blocking future improvement and unowned vague concern.
conditions: The condition must prevent a named current transition, acceptance claim, readiness claim, or safe handoff.
Plan must stop at a blocked gate and preserve remediation guidance rather than silently changing mode or authority.

includes: A missing item, evidence or detail; its non-blocking rationale; owner; repair route; and escalation condition.
excludes: Conditions that already prevent acceptance, readiness, validation, or safe execution.
conditions: The current bounded claim must remain valid without the missing item.
A gap escalates to a blocker when it becomes acceptance-critical or invalidates the selected unit, evidence, topology, scope, or handoff.

includes: One mutation-capable SWU's terminal source receipt contract, exact synchronization target inventory, baseline binding, admitted delta classes, lifecycle-owner validation, expected owner receipt, and deterministic successor policy.
excludes: Implementation admission, another SWU, authority changes, promotion, publication, deployment, destructive cleanup, policy or cost-risk acceptance, and unrelated targets.
conditions: Every mutation-capable SWU must have one complete closeout contract before Task Session admission.
Missing inventory, baseline, delta classes, validation, expected receipt, or deterministic successor policy blocks execution before source mutation.
Closeout must not infer undeclared targets after implementation.
A successor may be selected only when the contract identifies one unique dependency-ready same-Work-Pack successor; otherwise it selects none.

includes: The exact selected unit, dependencies, route, target, write and effect scope, required inputs, expected receipt, evidence, admission timing, entry state, risk ceiling, gate result, and stop conditions.
A finite ordered execution frontier and exact allowed internal-route projection.
excludes: Task execution, implicit unit or successor selection, a second route-level authorization prompt for matched internal routes, broader mutation authority, and pre-generated runtime context packs.
conditions: A task with multiple SWUs must select exactly one SWU before mutation-capable work starts.
Selection-ready means no unit is yet mutation-admitted and routes to the readiness owner rather than directly to Task Session.
The exact selected unit and current evidence must pass the installed entry and readiness checks before handoff.

Undeclared routes and product or semantic choice, scope expansion, destructive or irreversible effects, credentials, external messages or network effects, cost or risk acceptance, authority promotion, publication, deployment, and failed acceptance-critical validation stop before mutation.
A pre-execution owner prerequisite must bind its exact record and authorization evidence, return to the same Task Session attempt, and resume exactly once.
A declared same-route retry is limited to one repairable-owner-condition result for the unchanged entry and selected unit.

includes: The medium and high complexity choreography view for wave order, cross-task dependencies, stage coverage, closure obligations, SWU scheduling, and parallelization boundaries.
excludes: Source-of-truth task specifications, source-of-truth SWU definitions, independent execution state, and replacement of the Work Pack.
conditions: Medium and high complexity plans require an Execution Pack or a recorded blocker.
Every referenced wave, task, SWU, dependency, and layer assignment must agree with Work Pack source truth.
The Execution Pack schedules existing waves and SWUs and must not redefine their contracts.

consumer_topology.no_consumers_evidence: Not applicable: the current Plan contract and Work Pack template explicitly identify Task Session, Goal/runtime handoffs, runtime subagents, Work Pack Readiness Audit, and Implementation Readiness as downstream consumers.
